title: How Environmental Software Fits the Systems You Already Run
summary: Maintenance, historian, and EHS records can each be accurate. Environmental reporting still needs the data used, the method, and the review.
body_markdown:
Suppose maintenance has closed the work order for a compressor driver replacement, recorded under a new equipment identifier. Operations has the month’s readings in the historian, while the EHS platform contains an inspection record for that equipment. The environmental team still needs to establish how those records support the reporting calculation. IT has a related question: why can’t the systems already in place handle that work?


## Which existing systems can stay in place


Adding environmental software does not necessarily require replacing the systems already responsible for maintenance, operations, and EHS. The maintenance system may accurately record the equipment replacement, the historian may contain the relevant operating data, and the EHS platform may document the inspection. Those records alone may not explain which data and methods were used to calculate the reported emissions.


Records supporting the calculation and its review may already be maintained in an EHS platform, a dedicated environmental system, or across several systems. Before adding another system, the environmental team should ask whether the systems already in place can preserve the calculation, its supporting evidence, and the record of its review. Incomplete documentation alone does not mean new software is required.


## What each system is already for


Each system records information needed for its own operations, but those records may not explain which data was used in an environmental calculation, how it was calculated, or who reviewed the result.

## What happens to one environmental result


Following the compressor driver replacement, the environmental team needs to determine whether the change affects the source records used for reporting. The maintenance work order documents the replacement, but may not establish its implications for the reporting calculation. The team should retain which reporting source records were affected by the replacement and how that decision was reflected in the calculation.

If the question is whether a historian extract is fit to use, that is covered in[SCADA data for emissions reporting in oil and gas](https://blog.validere.com/scada-data-emissions-reporting-oil-and-gas) .


The monthly calculation may be approved in an email, with a spreadsheet attached, while an EHS task for the same equipment is marked complete. A reviewer who has only the email and the completed task may be unable to tell which activity and which method were reviewed. The review record should identify the calculation and supporting information that were approved.


If the underlying activity changes after that approval, the team should be able to identify the original figure and understand what changed. Whether the revised figure needs another review, another approval, or a new submission depends on the applicable reporting requirements and the company’s own procedures.

Without a consistent way to retrieve that information, the team may repeat the same checks and reconciliation work each reporting period. This takes time and makes it harder for another reviewer to understand how previous figures were produced.


## What to ask before adding environmental software


Before introducing another system, determine which parts of environmental reporting your existing tools already support and where manual work or missing records create problems.


Three questions can help:


1. **What can our existing systems already handle?** Identify where environmental calculations, supporting data, and approvals are currently managed, and whether those systems can support the reporting process without additional software.


2. **Can we identify and verify the data behind our reported figures?** Teams should be able to determine which operational data was used, where it originated, and which calculation method was applied.


3. **Can we explain previous results when information changes?** If source data is corrected or an equipment record changes, the team needs to identify what was originally reported, what changed, and whether further review is required.

## Frequently asked questions


### Can environmental software work alongside an existing ERP, historian, and EHS platform?


Yes. Environmental software can work alongside existing ERP, historian, and EHS systems. The question is whether the organization can maintain reliable links between the source data, calculations, and review records using its current systems or whether additional software is needed.

### How should teams handle corrected data after an environmental result has been approved?


Keep the original figure and a clear account of what changed. The team determines whether further review or resubmission is required under the applicable requirements and procedures.
